::: {.why}
Five sensitivities, each with a closed form and each computable numerically, and having both means every one of them is checked rather than trusted.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Implement delta, gamma, vega, theta and rho analytically and confirm each against a central finite difference.
- Say what each greek is a sensitivity to and which two are not derivatives with respect to a market variable.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Implement all five in qlib/derivatives/greeks.py and check each against a central finite difference of your own pricer across a grid of moneyness and maturity. Report the maximum relative discrepancy. The check catches the sign and factor errors that are otherwise invisible until a hedge loses money.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Note what vega and rho are: sensitivities to model parameters rather than to state variables, which means they measure model risk rather than market risk in a strict reading. Then plot delta and gamma against moneyness for three maturities and describe the shapes in words, since you will be asked to sketch them.
:::
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}

:::
